channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Fed’s Waller: Forward guidance can be “valuable tool” but may become a hindrance
item.description: Federal Reserve (Fed) Governor Christopher Waller said on Monday that forward guidance can strengthen the impact of monetary policy when used properly, but warned that it can also become problematic if it limits policymakers’ flexibility.

item.title: Australian Dollar trades sideways after softer Australian inflation
item.description: AUD/USD trades with a cautious tone, sideways near the 0.6930 level on Monday after Australian inflation data showed further easing price pressures, while mixed United States (US) services figures kept the US Dollar (USD) broadly supported but without strong momentum.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Sideways trade within defined band against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang indicates USD/CNH has seen a slight softening in momentum but remains confined to a narrow intraday band of 6.7800–6.7930. Over the next 1–3 weeks, the bank expects range trading between 6.7750 and 6.8080 as earlier Dollar strength has faded.

item.title: LatAm FX: Rotation favors equities and carry – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu notes that crowded exposure to Latin American (LatAm) bonds is unwinding as higher U.S. yields drive a domestic repricing of real-rate risks. The bank sees flows rotating toward regional equities and maintains a constructive tactical view on Latin American carry.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD struggles below key SMAs despite easing Fed hike bets
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) pauses a four-day winning streak on Monday as buyers take a breather following last week's 5.55% rally. A firmer US Dollar (USD) is also capping the precious metal's upside.

item.title: Canadian Dollar dips despite rising Oil prices amid firm US Dollar
item.description: USD/CAD extends its advance for a second consecutive day and trades around 1.4230 at the time of writing on Monday, up 0.20% on the day.

item.title: Euro: Soft tone against US Dollar with stable ECB expectations – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note EUR/USD around 1.1418 trading softer against the US Dollar, though mid-pack within G10. Euro area Producer Price Index (PPI) and retail sales were in line with expectations, while German factory orders surprised higher.

item.title: Australian Dollar retreats toward 0.6900 amid renewed signs of cooling inflation
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) is confronting a notable shift in market momentum as fresh domestic data points to cooling inflation.

item.title: United States: Sideways growth, sticky inflation – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities projects US output growth to move sideways in 2026, slightly below trend, with Real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) at 2.0% Q4/Q4 and unemployment around 4.3%. The Iran conflict and an oil shock pose stagflationary risks, while AI and high-income consumers support demand.

item.title: Gold trades lower as Fed interest rate outlook remains in focus
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) consolidates losses on Monday as a firmer US Dollar (USD) and mild profit-taking cap gains following last week's rebound from a more than seven-month low of $3,941.

item.title: Germany: Gradual industrial recovery prospects – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Marco Wagner notes that German manufacturing orders rose 1.9% in May, or 1.0% excluding large orders, pointing to an upward trend. He argues this supports a moderate recovery in German industry and a slight recovery in the broader German economy after a likely small Q2 decline.

item.title: US ISM Services PMI eases to 54 in June
item.description: Economic activity in the US service sector lost some momentum in June, with the ISM Services PMI easing to 54.0 from 54.5 in the previous month, matching analysts' expectations.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Consolidation against US Dollar with limited gains – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret describe USD/CAD around 1.4215 as consolidating, with the Canadian Dollar retaining a soft undertone despite narrower US–Canada front-end spreads.

item.title: British Pound climbs to January 2008 high against Japanese Yen despite intervention risk
item.description: GBP/JPY edges higher on Monday, climbing to levels last seen in January 2008 as the Japanese Yen (JPY) remains under pressure across the board. The Yen resumed its decline after a brief pullback last week, with USD/JPY climbing back to its highest level in four decades.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Testing major support with rebound risk against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts describe AUD/USD extending its pullback after breaking below the May trough around 0.7070 and retesting the 200-DMA near 0.6870/0.6830, aligned with March lows. They stress this zone as key support, noting November 2025’s correction also held there.

item.title: Oil: Supply normalization pressures prices – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu notes that OPEC+ has ratified another production quota increase, extending gradual supply normalization and adding pressure on Brent and WTI.

item.title: Euro: Resilient data backs range rebound against US Dollar – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman highlights that EUR/USD is trading just above 1.1400, testing the bottom of its 1.1400–1.1800 range. The Euro has faced selling on weaker data and reduced ECB hike expectations, but recent indicators show resilience.

item.title: Fed: Data-dependent hold stance – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Oscar Munoz and Eli Nir expect the Federal Reserve to keep the Fed funds rate on hold throughout 2026 as US growth moves sideways and inflation stays elevated.

item.title: Reserve Bank of New Zealand: Insurance hike risk balance – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole expects the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) to deliver a 25bp ‘insurance’ hike in July, taking the policy rate to 2.50%, despite the sharp drop in Oil prices.

item.title: Turkish Lira: Inflation momentum still too strong – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose notes that June Turkish Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Producer Price Index (PPI) data were better than expected as the energy shock faded, with headline CPI slowing to 32.1% year-on-year and PPI to 28.1%.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Softer inflation challenges RBA stance – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu reports that Australia’s Melbourne Institute inflation gauge fell again in June, with both headline and trimmed mean measures easing.

item.title: US Dollar: Rally pause seen as temporary – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists Kit Juckes and Olivier Korber argue that Dollar strength remains underpinned by robust US growth, sticky inflation and a favourable terms of trade shock versus Europe and Asia.

item.title: Euro: Range-bound against US Dollar under Fed support – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner says EUR/USD is consolidating above 1.1400 as markets reassess European Central Bank (ECB) and Fed paths, with a September ECB hike priced below 50% probability.

item.title: 162.30: Japanese Yen falls back to near 40-year lows as intervention risks loom
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) has resumed its broader downtrend against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday following a mild relief last week.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Weakness and intervention risks persist against US Dollar – HSBC
item.description: HSBC strategists argue that the USD/JPY pair is trading near its highest level in around 40 years and may have shifted into a new, higher range.

item.title: WTI Oil falls as oversupply concerns outweigh recent rebound
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil trades around $68.30 at the time of writing on Monday, down 0.64% on the day, as investors continue to assess the global supply outlook following the latest production decisions by the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and its allies (OPEC+).

item.title: Euro remains depressed against British Pound despite positive Eurozone data
item.description: The Euro (EUR) remains depressed near one-year lows against the British Pound (GBP) on Monday, hitting session lows below 0.8560 after pulling back from Friday’s highs at 0.8575.

item.title: Euro: Choppy range outlook against US Dollar – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley notes that EUR/USD recently fell below its prior 1‑month forecast of 1.15, prompting a reassessment of projections.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD struggles to extend recovery above 20-day EMA
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) is down 0.8% to near $4,140 during the European trading session on Monday. The precious metal faces selling pressure as the three-day rally hits a pause after failing to extend above $4,202.

item.title: British Pound: Sterling strength on positioning and flows – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale notes that Sterling has been the strongest G10 currency since the Makerfield by-election, helped by a still-sizeable but reduced speculative short base.
